title: A practitioner’s 2026 LLM review finds coding agents crossed a usability threshold
friendlyTitle: A clear guide to what changed in AI during 2026
summary: Simon Willison’s annotated keynote traces the year’s model, coding-agent, security and tool-use developments. His central practical observation is that late-2025 model improvements made coding agents reliable enough for daily use, while 2026 exposed both their wider usefulness and their security limits.
friendlySummary: Developer Simon Willison reviews the year’s important models, coding agents and security lessons. He argues that coding agents became dependable enough for everyday work, but still need careful limits.
whyItMatters: The review is a useful map for deciding what changed materially rather than chasing every release. Its working method is equally valuable: use agents ambitiously, sandbox them, inspect their output and learn their limits through real projects.
friendlyWhyItMatters: The guide helps separate important changes from launch noise. Its practical advice is to try agents on real work while checking their output and keeping them inside safe boundaries.
